solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: High street store's opening? Ask which is the best

indicators.note: high means drunk or intoxicated, so the letters that follow are reeling into a new order

parts.note: the word street as written, plus the opening letter of the word store

explanation.surface: A shopper wonders which shop on the high street to try, and is told to consult the experts about the top choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High' looks like part of 'High street', but it is the anagram signal: STREET plus S (the opening of 'store's') plus ASKWHICH are rearranged. Which? is a British consumer magazine that rates products.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: something described as the cat's whiskers is the very finest, top of its class.

clue.text: Literal mind oddly rejected taking drug for disease

indicators.note: taking says the word for literal takes in the letter for drug

parts.note: a literal is a printing error, a typo
H is slang for heroin

indicators.note: oddly rejected discards the odd-placed letters of mind, keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: A printing slip leaves a mind ill, after which a drug is taken for the disease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Literal' is a noun here: printers' slang for a misprint.
explanation.definitionFit: Typhoid fever is a bacterial infection spread by contaminated food and water.

clue.text: eBay's upset about a TV I flogged? That's awakening memories!

indicators.note: upset says the e-bay letters are broken open to take something in

parts.note: split as e plus bay, with voe a Shetland word for a bay or inlet
C is short for circa, about

indicators.note: flogged, beaten about, signals that a TV I is rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone stirs up old memories by selling an old TV on eBay.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'eBay' as E plus BAY, and a voe is a Shetland inlet. 'flogged' mixes A TV I into ATIV; 'upset' opens EVOE to take C plus ATIV.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that calls up memories or feelings vividly is evocative.

clue.text: Lower one's voice when speaking

indicators.note: when speaking says the words are said aloud to give a different spelling

parts.note: one gives A, the indefinite article; a deep male singing voice is a bass

explanation.surface: Advice to drop one's voice during a talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower' is not about volume but humbling: to lower oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to degrade or humiliate someone is to lower them in rank or esteem.

clue.text: Services initially slashed by elected Government, creating offence

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of Services

parts.note: slash is British slang for urinate, so slashed is peed
a party elected is in

explanation.surface: Public services cut by a newly elected government cause offence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slashed' is not about cuts but British slang for having urinated.
explanation.definitionFit: Driving over the limit is a motoring crime, an example of an offence.

clue.text: Raised a brief cheer at heart for basset hound

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the letters read upwards, backwards

parts.note: hurrah cut short is rah

indicators.note: at heart picks the central letters of basset

explanation.surface: A short cheer is raised for a basset hound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hound' looks like part of the dog breed, but it is a verb meaning pester.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to pester or persecute someone relentlessly is to hound them.

clue.text: Senior copper formerly county's rising star

parts.note: a superintendent, a senior police officer, is a super

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the letters read upwards, backwards

parts.note: Avon was an English county abolished in 1996

explanation.surface: A senior police officer once from the county is a rising star.
explanation.walkthrough: Avon was a county in south-west England from 1974 to 1996.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a massive exploding star that suddenly brightens is one kind of star.

clue.text: Sweat, being examined by university dean? Not half!

parts.note: ex. is a dictionary abbreviation for examined

indicators.note: not half says only half of the word dean is kept

explanation.surface: A student sweats while being examined by the university dean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' reads as an exclamation of agreement, but it halves 'dean' to DE.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to give off moisture through the skin is to exude or sweat.

clue.text: Outline omits an English poet

indicators.note: omits says one letter is removed from the word for outline

parts.note: a skeleton is an outline or framework
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A literary summary leaves out a certain English poet.
explanation.walkthrough: John Skelton was a Tudor poet, tutor to the young Henry VIII.
explanation.definitionFit: John Skelton (c.1463 to 1529) was an English poet known for his short rhyming lines.

clue.text: Inclined to hold nothing sacred? The opposite

indicators.note: to hold says the word for inclined wraps around the word for nothing

parts.note: inclined, as in disposed or liable, means prone
sweet FA is British slang for nothing at all

explanation.surface: Someone is asked whether they tend to respect nothing at all, and the reply is a contradiction.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole tail: the opposite of sacred. FA (from 'sweet FA') is British slang for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: An antonym: what is irreverent and worldly stands against what is holy, so this is sacred's opposite.

clue.text: Runs to catch first departing transport

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: first departing says the opening letter of the word for catch goes

parts.note: to catch is to capture

explanation.surface: Someone sprints to make the first bus or train leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transport' is not a vehicle here but a state of delight, as in 'transports of joy'.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to be in transports is to be carried away by ecstasy or bliss.

clue.text: To give speech in front of class is nothing

indicators.note: in front of puts the letter for nothing ahead of the word for class

parts.note: O, the round figure zero, stands for nothing
a rate is a class or grade, as in first-rate

explanation.surface: A pupil must address the class, which feels like nothing to them.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to deliver a formal address or declaim is to give a speech.

clue.text: Bad directions lacking clarity principally will do this?

definitions.text: Bad directions lacking clarity principally will do this?

indicators.note: bad signals that the letters of directions are spoiled into another order
lacking says a letter is removed from directions before rearranging
principally picks the first letter of clarity

explanation.surface: Poor, unclear directions will leave a traveller confused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' takes C (the first letter of 'clarity') out of DIRECTIONS, and 'Bad' rearranges what is left. The whole clue is also the definition: muddled directions confuse you.
explanation.definitionFit: To confuse someone about their position or bearings is exactly what vague instructions do.

clue.text: Daughter's excellent roasts may make one this fat

definitions.text: roasts may make one this fat

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter
ripping is old British slang for excellent

explanation.surface: A daughter's superb roast dinners might fatten someone up.
explanation.walkthrough: Ripping is dated British slang for splendid. The definition reads as 'make one fat', but it is the fat that roasting meat gives off.
explanation.definitionFit: Fat that melts out of meat as it roasts is collected and used for cooking, a British kitchen staple.

clue.text: Plucked energy up to stay in command in South Africa

indicators.note: stay in says the South Africa piece is kept inside the others
up in a down clue means the letters read upwards, backwards

parts.note: zip is energy or vigour

indicators.note: in says the command letters sit inside the South Africa letters

parts.note: ZA is the international code for South Africa
IC means in command, in charge

explanation.surface: A burst of energy is needed to stay in command in South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plucked' refers to strings, not feathers: a direction to play by plucking.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical term for playing a bowed string instrument by plucking the strings with the fingers.

clue.text: Reel requires goin' up and down

definitions.meaning: a reel is a spool for winding thread
moving up and down with the final g dropped, as the apostrophe in goin' shows

explanation.surface: A spool, it seems, demands constant bouncing.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is the answer with a dropped g, as the apostrophe in 'goin'' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: A spool on which thread or yarn is wound is a reel; the colloquial form means bouncing.

clue.text: School over in London area could be something attractive

indicators.note: in puts the turned school inside the London area

parts.note: Barnet is a borough of north London

indicators.note: over says the word for school is turned around

parts.note: a gam is a school of whales

explanation.surface: A school in a London district might prove an attractive choice.
explanation.walkthrough: Barnet is an outer London borough. 'School' is a group of whales, not a place of learning.
explanation.definitionFit: A straight magnet attracts iron, so it is literally something attractive.

clue.text: I seek a bloomer extremely desperately one of these may have one

definitions.text: one of these may have one

indicators.note: desperately signals the letters are thrown about into a new order
extremely picks the two end letters of bloomer

explanation.surface: Someone desperately hunts for a bloomer, a type of loaf.
explanation.walkthrough: A bloomer is a British crusty loaf, so a bread shop may stock one.
explanation.definitionFit: Shops that bake and sell bread would stock a bloomer, a large crusty British loaf.

clue.text: Succeeded with lie about restricting European corruption

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded in family trees

indicators.note: restricting says the word for lie about confines the letter for European

parts.note: to lie about lazily is to laze

explanation.surface: A politician got away with a fib about curbing someone from Europe, and it smells of corruption.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: sordid dishonesty in public life, such as bribery, is called sleaze.

clue.text: Family member conceals current location in Wiltshire

indicators.note: conceals says the word for current is hidden within the family member

parts.note: a son is a member of the family
wind is a current of air

explanation.surface: A relative hides the present whereabouts of somewhere in Wiltshire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' is not 'present' but a flow of air.
explanation.definitionFit: Swindon is a large town in the English county of Wiltshire.

clue.text: Charlie has a party song about region of Italy

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: about says the word for song goes around the word for party

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in opera
Lab is short for Labour, the British political party

explanation.surface: Charlie throws a party with singing to celebrate an Italian region.
explanation.definitionFit: Calabria is the toe of the Italian boot, a southern region of the country.

clue.text: A special fizzy drink's heading off sterility

indicators.note: heading off says the first letter of the drink goes

parts.note: Pepsi is a fizzy cola, with the s from the possessive

explanation.surface: A special fizzy drink is heading off a sterility problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Asepsis is the absence of germs, the sterile condition kept in surgery.

clue.text: Kohl could be part of this constitution

definitions.text: Kohl could be part of this
definitions.meaning: kohl is eye cosmetic, so it is part of cosmetics
constitution as in one's basic character or nature

explanation.surface: Helmut Kohl might help shape a nation's constitution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kohl' looks like Helmut Kohl, the German chancellor, but it is dark eye cosmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: cosmetics applied to the face, and a person's inner nature or composition.

clue.text: Incriminate one politician, a whip involved in deceit

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: involved in says the word for whip sits inside the word for deceit

parts.note: a lie is a deceit
the cat o' nine tails was a whip, called the cat

explanation.surface: A politician and a party whip are caught up in a scandal of deception.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whip' is not the party official the surface suggests but the cat o' nine tails.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to show someone is involved in a crime is to implicate or incriminate them.

clue.text: Priest once more saving one unbeliever

indicators.note: saving means except, so one letter is left out of the word for once more

parts.note: again means once more
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A priest tries again to save an unbeliever's soul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saving' means 'except', not rescuing a soul.
explanation.definitionFit: A heathen who follows no mainstream religion is a nonbeliever, an unbeliever.

clue.text: To find fault with Britain's unfashionable in America

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for Britain
lame is American slang for uncool or unfashionable

explanation.surface: A Brit is criticised for being out of step with American style.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to censure or hold someone responsible is to find fault with them.

clue.text: To misrepresent is essential to libel, I explain

indicators.note: essential to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A lawyer explains that misrepresentation is central to libel.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to give a false impression of something is to misrepresent it.

clue.text: Humble pie of rag's hacking editors making comeback

indicators.note: hacking says the mixed-up rag cuts into the editors' letters
making comeback says the editors' letters are read backwards

parts.note: ED is the abbreviation for editor, so two editors give ED twice

indicators.note: pie is printers' jargon for jumbled type, so pie of rag means rag mixed up

parts.note: rag is used as written before mixing

explanation.surface: Editors eat humble pie when their tabloid's hacking scandal returns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Humble pie' looks like one phrase, but only 'Humble' is the definition. 'pie of' is printers' jargon for jumbled type; 'hacking' cuts it into the two editors, which 'making comeback' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to lower someone's dignity or standing is to humble or debase them.

clue.text: One son comes down for Christmas and Easter, perhaps

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
an aircraft that comes down lands

explanation.surface: A son flies home for the holidays.
explanation.walkthrough: Christmas Island and Easter Island are both real places, so the festivals are examples of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Examples: Christmas Island in the Indian Ocean and Easter Island in the Pacific are both pieces of land in the sea.

clue.text: Maybe corporal punishment's introduction sorted out sons with time? That's insane!

parts.note: a corporal is an example of a non-commissioned officer, a noncom

indicators.note: introduction picks the first letter of punishment's
sorted out says the letters of sons and time are rearranged

explanation.surface: Corporal punishment applied to sons is said to have straightened them out in time, a view the clue calls mad.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin legal phrase meaning not of sound mind, used for someone mentally unfit.
